extracts.section: RISK FACTORS, data center capacity table, notes
extracts.quote: (1) Built Capacity is the maximum IT load a data center is engineered to support, based on business requirements, space planning, and infrastructure feasibility. This has been calculated based on the present design specifications in the respective data centers, using total planned electrical load and design power density. (2) Installed Capacity is the portion of built capacity that is equipped, powered and commissioned for operation. This has been calculated based on the present equipment installed in the respective data centers. (3) Operational Capacity is the total IT power capacity that has been sold to customers during the year / periods for which revenue from operations is generated. This has been calculated based on contracted load or committed IT power sold to customers. (4) Capacity utilization is the operational capacity as a percentage of installed capacity.
extracts.finding: The prospectus headline reports a built IT power capacity of 188.04 MW. Its own footnote defines built capacity as what a facility is engineered to support, from design specifications and planned electrical load. The word built therefore carries a design meaning in this document.

extracts.section: OBJECTS OF THE OFFER, Chennai 02 Data Center
extracts.quote: Other technical facilities at the Chennai 02 Data Center include 4 diverse fiber paths and an on-side 230 kV GIS substation, which helps ensure uninterrupted, high-capacity power supply.
extracts.note: A 230 kV substation is a transmission level connection, which is the point at which the grid register and the accounts register touch.

extracts.quote: According to the 1Lattice and C&W Report, factors like rising digitalization and AI adoption are expected to push data center demand in India from current levels of 1.3 GW in Fiscal 2025 to between 4.7 GW to 5.7 GW in Fiscal 2030
extracts.note: A commissioned third party forecast, not an audited figure. Treat as SECONDARY.
